Let’s evaluate each option step by step.  

**(A)** Ammonia is produced in repeated high intensity exercise.  
True — during intense exercise, AMP deamination in the purine nucleotide cycle produces ammonia.  

**(B)** Muscle lactate accumulation does not begin until at least 5 seconds of intermittent muscle contractions have taken place.  
This seems suspicious — lactate can start accumulating very quickly (within a few seconds) if glycolysis is rapid and oxidative phosphorylation can’t keep up. Waiting until “at least 5 seconds” is arbitrary and likely false; lactate accumulation can begin earlier.  

**(C)** Muscle phosphocreatine depletion begins in the first few seconds of high intensity exercise.  
True — phosphocreatine hydrolysis starts immediately to replenish ATP.  

**(D)** With an increasing number of repeated sprints the rate of accumulation of lactate in muscle declines.  
True — due to lower power output in later sprints, less glycogen availability, or other metabolic adaptations, lactate accumulation rate can decrease.  

Thus, the false statement is **(B)**.  

Final answer: (B)
